metaDescription: Six swivel power recliners compared on swivel angle, glider motion, seat width, massage and fabric, to help you pick one that fits your room.
introParagraphs: A swivel power recliner adds a rotating base to the usual push-button recline, so the chair can turn toward a window, a television or a visitor without dragging it across the floor. Many models also glide or rock, which makes them popular for nurseries as well as living rooms. For adults who want a chair that moves with them, the extra motion is the main draw.

The six chairs below range from a fabric glider with a 240-degree turn to oversized models with massage, heat and a 270-degree rotation. We evaluated them from product specs and buyer feedback rather than claiming hands-on testing. Swivel range, seat width, how the rocking is controlled and what the cover is made of separate them more than the shared remote does.

These are comfort chairs, not medical devices, and a moving base needs extra care. Weight capacity, a level floor and correct assembly all matter, and an occupational or physical therapist can advise when mobility or transfers are a concern. A chair that swings or rocks should be steadied before anyone stands up from it.

products.name: Ketaiyou Power Swivel Rocker Recliner, Dark Grey
products.description:
The Ketaiyou is the most complete all-rounder in this group. It rotates 270 degrees, rocks, reclines electrically between 90 and 160 degrees and adds massage with heat. Dual side pockets, two cup holders and built-in USB complete the package.

The broad recline range gives it more reach than the Delta Mercer, which is a smaller, simpler glider. Combined features add weight and parts, so the chair is a more considerable purchase than a basic rocker. If you only want to swivel, you may be paying for functions you will not use.

In ownership, plan floor space around the base so the swivel is free to turn. The rocking can be a plus for relaxing, but be sure it has stopped moving before standing. A second Coffee colour of the same model is also listed, so choose by room colour rather than by function.

pros: 270-degree swivel turns toward a window or door
Recline spans 90 to 160 degrees
Side pockets and two cup holders included
Massage, heat and USB in one chair
cons: More parts and weight than a basic glider
Rocking should be settled before standing

products.name: ANJ Dual Motor Oversized Swivel Rocker Recliner
products.description:
The ANJ is the heavyweight of the lineup, listed with a 400 lb capacity and two motors. One motor moves the backrest and footrest together, and the second adjusts the headrest. It swivels 270 degrees, rocks, and adds an eight-point vibration massage with lumbar heat.

A cup holder, two armrest storage compartments and a phone or tablet holder keep devices close. The tradeoff is size and weight, so check the doorway and the room before ordering. The adjustable headrest is useful for people who rest their neck while reading or watching a screen.

Because weight capacity is the highest here, it is the natural option for larger frames. Compared with the Bonzy's 23.2-inch seat, the ANJ is listed as oversized, though the listing gives no seat width. Always confirm the capacity on the final dimension sheet.
products.bestFor: Larger users who need a high listed capacity and a powered headrest.
pros: Listed capacity of 400 lbs is the highest here
Dual motors add a powered headrest
Phone or tablet holder and armrest storage
Eight vibration points with lumbar heat
cons: Heavy and bulky to move into place

products.name: Delta Children Mercer Power Recliner and Swivel Glider
products.description:
The Mercer is a glider first and a recliner second. It swivels 240 degrees, glides on a metal base, reclines electronically to any position and includes a USB port. LiveSmart performance fabric is described as stain resistant and water resistant, and the frame is a durable wood build.

The gliding motion is smooth and quiet, which suits shared spaces where noise matters. It lacks the massage and heat found on the Ketaiyou and RUTOX, so it feels simpler and less gadget-heavy. The 240-degree swivel is also narrower than the 270 degrees offered by the other chairs here.

Performance fabric handles everyday spills better than typical upholstery, though it still needs prompt blotting. The glider base needs forward clearance, and anyone sitting down should let it settle first. It suits a nursery, a bedroom or a quiet corner with limited space.
products.bestFor: Quiet rooms where a stain-resistant glider with USB matters most.
pros: LiveSmart fabric is stain and water resistant
Glides quietly on a metal base
Electronic recline stops at any position
USB port is built in beside the recline control
cons: No massage or heat functions on this glider
Swivel is 240 degrees, narrower than rivals

products.name: RUTOX Oversized Swivel Rocker Recliner with Massage
products.description:
The RUTOX combines the features of a swivel rocker and a glider recliner in one oversized chair. It rotates 270 degrees, reclines electrically and offers eight vibration massage nodes across the back, lumbar area and legs, with lumbar heating alongside. A customizable headrest and a roomy seat padded with thick high-density foam round it out.

The adjustable headrest is a clear advantage for anyone who is taller than average. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no seat width, no weight rating and no recline angle, so these must be checked on the dimension sheet. A similar RUTOX listing appears in the market, so confirm the model name before buying.

In ownership, soft foam and a wider seat mean the chair is heavy to move once set up. Compared with the Ketaiyou, the RUTOX highlights the headrest, while the Ketaiyou lists a clear recline range. Keep the floor clear around the swivel.
products.bestFor: Taller buyers who want an adjustable headrest and oversized comfort.
pros: Adjustable headrest suits taller sitters
Eight nodes cover back, lumbar and legs
High-density foam padding on seat and arms
270-degree swivel and glide in one chair
cons: Capacity and recline angle are not given
Large chair is hard to reposition

products.name: SINCRUMI Power Swivel Rocker Recliner with Vibration
products.description:
The SINCRUMI offers a 270-degree swivel, a 160-degree recline and 30 degrees of rocking. Heating elements target the lower back, and vibration offers five modes, eight vibrations and four custom zone settings across the back and other areas.

The zone settings give more control than a single on-off vibration, which suits people who want only the lower back or only the legs. It is the only chair in this lineup that publishes both a recline and a rocking figure, which helps when planning space. The tradeoff is a busy remote with several modes to learn.

Ownership is similar to other swivel rockers: keep clear space, level floor and a nearby outlet. Against the Ketaiyou's 90 to 160 degrees, the SINCRUMI matches the maximum recline but adds an explicit rocking angle. It lacks the armrest storage listed on the ANJ.
products.bestFor: Buyers who like to pick massage zones and know the rocking angle in advance.
pros: Both recline and rocking angles are published
Four zone settings target specific areas
Five vibration modes for varied intensity
Heating element focuses on the lower back
cons: Several modes make the remote busier
No armrest storage mentioned in the listing

products.name: Bonzy Home Power Swivel Rocker Recliner with USB
products.description:
The Bonzy has a 23.2-inch seat, which the listing says is wider than a standard nursery chair, plus fixed lumbar support, a 270-degree swivel and a gentle rocking motion. A USB port is included, and the upholstered glider design is aimed at living rooms as well as nurseries.

It keeps the feature set modest, with no massage or heat. A fixed lumbar support means the backrest shape does not change, so people who prefer to adjust should test one in person if possible. The 23.2-inch width is the clearest stated seat measurement in this group.

It is a calmer, simpler choice than the SINCRUMI or ANJ. Compared with the Mercer, the Bonzy swivels 270 degrees instead of 240, though it does not mention stain-resistant fabric. Keep floor space around the base so the swivel can turn freely.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a straightforward swivel glider with a stated seat width.
pros: Stated 23.2-inch seat width is easy to compare
Fixed lumbar support gives a steady back shape
270-degree swivel with gentle rocking
USB port built in for phones and tablets
cons: No massage or heat functions on this model

buyingCriteria.explanation: Swivel range tells you how far the chair turns before it reaches a limit. The Ketaiyou, ANJ, RUTOX, SINCRUMI and Bonzy turn 270 degrees, while the Delta Mercer turns 240 degrees. A wider turn is useful in a room with a window and a television on different walls. Look for a stop or lock that keeps the base steady while you sit down or stand.

Rocking tilts the chair on a curved frame, while a glider slides on a track. The SINCRUMI lists 30 degrees of rocking, and the Delta Mercer glides on a metal base. Motion is soothing for some and unsteady for others. Choose a chair with a way to stop or lock the movement before standing.

Capacity and width show how well the chair suits the person. The ANJ lists 400 lbs, and the Bonzy lists a 23.2-inch seat. Check the final dimension sheet because several listings leave these out. Include clothing and items in the lap when comparing to the rating. Swivel bases also put extra stress on the joint, so a generous margin below the listed limit is sensible.

Single-motor chairs move the backrest and footrest together, while dual-motor chairs separate them. The ANJ uses two motors for a powered headrest. The Ketaiyou and SINCRUMI both reach 160 degrees. More motors add comfort options and more parts to maintain.

Eight-point vibration shows up on the ANJ, RUTOX, Ketaiyou and SINCRUMI, while the Mercer and Bonzy skip it. Extras are comfort features, not therapy. A shorter remote is easier for some users. Check that heat has a shut-off.

The Mercer's LiveSmart fabric is described as stain and water resistant, which helps in busy rooms. Other covers vary, so read the care label. Glider bases collect dust and lint, so check clearance for a vacuum. Easy upkeep keeps the chair looking good for longer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Swivel and motion
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swivel angle, rocking angle and glide design. Most chairs turn 270 degrees, with the Mercer at 240, and the SINCRUMI publishes a 30-degree rock. We also noted which chairs describe how motion is controlled or stopped.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and size
howWeEvaluated.description: The ANJ stands out with a listed 400 lbs, and the Bonzy lists a 23.2-inch seat, which is a useful baseline when comparing widths. Many listings omit one or both figures. Missing data counted as a reason to verify rather than a verdict on the chair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Recline and motors
howWeEvaluated.description: Dual motors on the ANJ and 160-degree reclines on the Ketaiyou and SINCRUMI set the pace. We compared how each chair describes its mechanism. Simpler single-motor chairs earned credit for easier use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and upholstery
howWeEvaluated.description: Massage, heat, USB and cup holders were weighed against cleaning needs. The Mercer's stain-resistant fabric leads on upkeep, while the RUTOX leads on headrest adjustment. Buyer feedback on cover wear was considered.

howWeEvaluated.title: Positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: Ketaiyou is the all-rounder, ANJ is the capacity pick, Mercer the glider, RUTOX the headrest pick, SINCRUMI the rocking pick and Bonzy the simple seat. These are editorial judgments, not hands-on measurements.

howToChoose.intro: The two motions feel different and fit different rooms.

cards.label: Rocker
cards.text: A rocker tilts on curved runners, so the chair leans back and forth and needs space behind it. The Ketaiyou, ANJ, RUTOX, SINCRUMI and Bonzy move this way. Pick one if you like a noticeable sway and have clearance.

cards.label: Glider
cards.text: A glider slides on a track, so the movement is smoother and takes less room. The Delta Mercer uses a metal glider base. Pick one if you want a calmer, quieter motion in a nursery or bedroom.

howToChoose.note: Whichever style you choose, steady the chair before standing up from it. Rocking works best on a firm, level floor, and a thick rug can make the runners catch, so test the motion after the chair is in its final spot. If anyone in the household uses a cane or walker, keep the path to the chair free of the swing zone.

cards.text: Look for a swivel range that matches the angle between your television and window, a seat width that fits the user and a base that clears the rug. Check the clearance behind for rocking and in front for gliding. Level flooring keeps the swivel steady.

howToChoose.note: Check weight rating and warranty terms on the listing before paying for upgrades. Remember that some of these chairs also appear in a second colour under a near-identical title, so compare the model line carefully and make sure the capacity, seat width and motor count you read belong to the exact version you are ordering. If delivery is a concern, ask whether the chair arrives assembled or needs the swivel plate attached by two people.

faq.q: Is a swivel recliner safe for older adults?
faq.a: A moving base needs extra care, because swivel and rocking can shift under someone who is standing. Choose a chair with a stop or lock where possible and keep the floor level. An occupational or physical therapist can advise on whether this style suits a particular person.

faq.q: What is the difference between a swivel glider and a rocker recliner?
faq.a: A glider slides forward and back along a track, while a rocker tilts on curved runners. Gliders feel smoother and need less rear clearance. Check each listing to see which motion it describes.

faq.q: How much space does a swivel recliner need?
faq.a: Allow room around the base so it can turn without hitting a wall or table, plus clearance behind for recline. A 270-degree chair needs more open floor than a basic recliner. Measure the room and the doorway before ordering.

faq.q: Do swivel recliners work for larger people?
faq.a: Some do, if the listed capacity and seat width fit. The ANJ lists 400 lbs and the Bonzy lists a 23.2-inch seat. Always confirm the figures on the maker's sheet and include clothing and items in the lap.

faq.q: Can the rocking motion be turned off?
faq.a: That depends on the model, and the listing does not say for most chairs. Look for a lock or stop on the listing, and ask the seller if it is unclear. If a lock is missing, keep the chair away from places where a sudden sway could cause trouble.

faq.q: How do I care for a swivel recliner?
faq.a: Wipe the cover according to the label, vacuum around the base and keep the cord out of the swivel path. Check bolts now and then, since moving bases can loosen over time. Contact the maker if the swivel grinds or the recline stalls.

faq.q: Can a swivel recliner replace a nursery glider?
faq.a: Several of these chairs are marketed for both nurseries and living rooms, including the Mercer and the Bonzy. A nursery chair is often judged on quiet motion and stain resistance, so the glider base and performance fabric on the Mercer are relevant. If the chair will also be used by adults for long periods, check the seat width and the capacity figure as well. Make sure any motion is stopped before standing or lifting a child.
